subject: VAL
label: Grade 11 Science
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 11 Science Values and life skills, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 2 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Values, ethics and wellbeing
modules.outcome: apply an ethical framework to a case
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Values, ethics and wellbeing', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: apply an ethical framework to a case. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Values, ethics and wellbeing' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: apply an ethical framework to a case. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: Calm routine: name the feeling, breathe in for 4 counts and out for 6, talk to someone, do one small helpful thing. Plan screen time: 1 hour, then a 10-minute break. Method: Model run for 'Values, ethics and wellbeing'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Apply an ethical framework to a case: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Learn three lenses. Consequences asks which choice gives the best result for the people affected. Duties asks which rules or promises, such as honest reporting, must be kept. Character asks what an honest, careful scientist would do. Use all three on a case.

Step 2, Read a science case. A student records 10 readings: 9.8, 9.7, 9.9, 9.8, 9.6, 9.7, 9.8, 12.4, 9.9, 9.7. The mean is 100.3 divided by 10, which is 10.03. Without 12.4 it is 9.77. The student wonders about deleting the odd value quietly.

Step 3, Apply consequences. Hiding the value makes the result look cleaner but may mislead readers and later work. Keeping it and saying it may be an error is honest and lets others judge. Short-term neatness costs long-term trust in the result.

Step 4, Apply duties and character. A scientist has a duty to report data truthfully, to give a reason for any exclusion and to keep the original record. A careful, honest person would check the instrument, repeat the reading and report both versions.

Step 5, Decide and justify. Write: 'Report all 10 readings, mark 12.4 as a possible outlier, and give both means with a reason.' The median is 9.8 either way, which is useful because it hardly changes. Doing this protects your wellbeing too, since nothing needs hiding.

Step 6, Your turn: readings 4.1, 4.0, 4.2, 4.1 and 6.0 add up to 22.4. Find the mean and say what to do with 6.0. Answer: the mean is 4.48; keep 6.0 in the record, flag it, check the instrument and report with and without it.

modules.example: Solved: List 3 strengths, 3 interests and 3 job families; match one to a course and write a next step with a date. Method: Model run for 'Career and higher-study pathways'. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Map interests to courses and careers: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Self-assessment: Rami rates his interests from 1 to 5: Biology 5, Chemistry 4, Maths 3, Helping people 4. Evidence: top marks in biology, a first-aid course, and a volunteer day at a care home.
Step 2, Course profiles: Weights for biology, chemistry, maths, helping. Nursing 0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5. Pharmacy 0.2, 0.5, 0.1, 0.2. Engineering 0.0, 0.2, 0.6, 0.2. Each row sums to 1.
Step 3, Score Nursing: 5 times 0.3 is 1.5; 4 times 0.1 is 0.4; 3 times 0.1 is 0.3; 4 times 0.5 is 2.0. Total is 1.5 plus 0.4 plus 0.3 plus 2.0, which is 4.2 out of 5.

Step 4, Score the others: Pharmacy is 1.0 plus 2.0 plus 0.3 plus 0.8, which is 4.1. Engineering is 0.0 plus 0.8 plus 1.8 plus 0.8, which is 3.4. Nursing 4.2 and Pharmacy 4.1 are very close, so the scores cannot separate them.

Step 5, Break the tie with evidence: Rami reads entry needs for each, shadows a nurse and a pharmacist for a day, and notes which tasks he enjoys: talking with patients or preparing and checking medicines. A near-tie means gather more evidence.

Step 6, Plan: He keeps both on a shortlist, checks the chemistry and biology marks needed, and plans a second work-shadow day. He writes that the pathway is a science degree followed by professional licensing, and checks the details with a counsellor.

Your turn: Ratings Biology 2, Chemistry 3, Maths 5, Helping 3 with Engineering weights 0.0, 0.2, 0.6, 0.2. Model answer: 0.0 plus 0.6 plus 3.0 plus 0.6 is 4.2 out of 5, a strong match worth exploring.

ladder: L1: kindness, honesty and sharing in daily life.
L2: responsibility, courage and care for others and nature.
L3: fairness, respect for difference and service.
L5: leadership, wellbeing and ethical reasoning.
L6 (degree): applied ethics, culture and community work.
L7 (postgraduate): scholarship, counselling or teaching at depth.
